# Functions

Functions are called from expressions (05 §4.7, §12). A random one draws from the rule stream and is refused in a pure context; one that is not *safe for belief* is refused in a mind context, where a character decides by what it has perceived (05 §7.3). Functions mods define are listed in their own files, not here.

## Combat

<a id="aside-from"></a>
### `aside_from`

`aside_from(who: any, from: any, right?: bool) -> string?` · safe for belief

The step that takes `who` across the line from `from`, out of the way of what comes along it (07 §5.2, §11.6): `north`, `north_east`, … to the left of someone facing straight away from `from`, or with `right` true to the right. Null for two in one column, or either nowhere. Safe for belief, as `away_from` is.

- `who` (any): Who steps: an entity or a cell.
- `from` (any): What it steps out of the line of: an entity or a cell.
- `right` (bool, optional): Whether to step to the right rather than the left. Default false.

<a id="contest"></a>
### `contest`

`contest(contest: id<contest>, a: real, b: real) -> real?` · safe for belief · random

A margin of a contest (07 §4.1): the scaled difference, or log-ratio, of `a` and `b`, plus logistic noise of the contest's spread drawn from the rule stream. At or above zero, `a` won. Refused in a pure context. Null for a value that is null.

- `contest` (id<contest>): The contest.
- `a` (real): The value of the side the margin favours when it is positive.
- `b` (real): The value of the other side.

<a id="odds"></a>
### `odds`

`odds(contest: id<contest>, a: real, b: real) -> real?` · safe for belief

The chance that a margin of a contest is at or above zero (07 §4.1), from 0 to 1. Pure: it draws nothing. Null for a value that is null.

- `contest` (id<contest>): The contest.
- `a` (real): The value of the side the margin favours.
- `b` (real): The value of the other side.

<a id="strike-preview"></a>
### `strike_preview`

`strike_preview(who: entity, action: any, target: entity, part?: any, effort?: real, attack?: string) -> map<any>?` · not in a mind context

What a strike of an attack of an action would likely do, worked out without drawing anything or changing anything (07 §13, invariant C5): `in_reach` (bool), `odds` (real, the chance it lands on the part aimed at), `odds_near` (real, on it or a part beside it), `energy` (real, joules of harm at the effort, less the push), `intensity` (real, pascals), `push_speed` (real, metres a second), `staggers` and `launches` (bool). Reads the target as it is: not safe for belief. Null for an action with no such attack, or with nothing to strike with.

- `who` (entity): Who would strike.
- `action` (any): The action: its id.
- `target` (entity): Whom it would strike.
- `part` (any, optional): The part aimed at, of the kind `part`; null for none.
- `effort` (real, optional): The effort, 0 to 1. Default 1.
- `attack` (string, optional): The attack's id; left out for an action with one.

## Maths

<a id="abs"></a>
### `abs`

`abs(x: number) -> number` · safe for belief

- `x` (number): A number.

The angle in radians, from -pi to pi, of the point (x, y) measured from the positive x axis.

<a id="ceil"></a>

`ceil(x: number) -> int` · safe for belief

### `clamp`

`clamp(x: number, low: number, high: number) -> number` · safe for belief

`x` limited to the range from `low` to `high`. If `low` is greater than `high` the result is `high`. An int if all three are ints.

- `x` (number): The number to limit.

- `high` (number): The most it may be.

`div(a: int, b: int) -> int` · safe for belief

- `b` (real): The value at `t` = 1.

## Perception

<a id="could-perceive"></a>
### `could_perceive`

`could_perceive(a: entity, at: any, kind: string) -> bool?` · not in a mind context

Whether a signal of a kind at a place would reach `a` now through one of its senses (15 §6). Null for a place, an entity or a kind that names nothing.

- `a` (entity): Who would perceive.
- `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `kind` (string): The signal kind's id, qualified or bare.

<a id="perceives"></a>
### `perceives`

`perceives(a: entity, b: entity) -> bool?` · not in a mind context · reactive

Whether `a` has `b` detected now (15 §6). Null if either is not an entity. Window kinds use `perceives(self, source)` as their `noticed_if`.

- `a` (entity): Who perceives.
- `b` (entity): Whom or what.

Its result changes on `detected`, `lost_track`.

## Random

<a id="chance"></a>
### `chance`

`chance(p: real) -> bool` · safe for belief · random

True with probability `p`. Zero or less is never; one or more is always.

- `p` (real): A probability from 0 to 1.

<a id="pick"></a>
### `pick`

`pick(list: list<any>) -> any` · safe for belief · random

One element of a list, each equally likely. Null for an empty list.

- `list` (list<any>): The list to choose from.

<a id="rand"></a>
### `rand`

`rand(a: real, b: real) -> real` · safe for belief · random

A random real from `a` up to but not including `b`.

- `a` (real): The least the result may be.
- `b` (real): The result is less than this.

<a id="rand-int"></a>
### `rand_int`

`rand_int(a: int, b: int) -> int` · safe for belief · random

A random int from `a` to `b`, both included. `a` if `b` is less than `a`.

- `a` (int): The least the result may be.
- `b` (int): The most the result may be.

## Ranged combat

<a id="ballistic-dir"></a>
### `ballistic_dir`

`ballistic_dir(from: any, to: any, speed: real) -> list<real>?` · not in a mind context

The direction, east, south and up, of length one, that sends a shot at `speed` from `from` down onto `to` under the gravity where `from` is, along the lower of the two arcs, with no drag (07 §11.4). An entity is taken at the height a shot leaves it from, a cell at its floor, and a list of three numbers as a point in metres. Null where no arc reaches it at that speed.

- `from` (any): Where the shot leaves from.
- `to` (any): Where it is to come down.
- `speed` (real): Its speed, in metres a second.

<a id="band-point"></a>
### `band_point`

`band_point(target: entity, part?: any) -> list<real>?` · not in a mind context

The point in metres, east, south and up in its grid, at the middle of the band of a part of an entity where it stands (07 §11.4); for no part, the middle of its body. Reads truth. Null for one not in the world.

- `target` (entity): Whose part.
- `part` (any, optional): The part, of the kind `part`; null for the middle of the body.

## Scenario

<a id="fallen"></a>
### `fallen`

`fallen() -> list<entity>` · safe for belief · reactive

The characters the player played who are gone, in the order they fell (13 §9.3). Empty with no game.

Its result changes on `control_changed`.

<a id="mission-state"></a>
### `mission_state`

`mission_state(mission: int) -> string?` · safe for belief · reactive

Where a mission of the game stands, by its number (13 §5.2): `active`, `done`, `failed` or `expired`; null if there is none.

- `mission` (int): The mission's number.

Its result changes on `mission_started`, `mission_done`, `mission_failed`, `mission_expired`.

<a id="objective-state"></a>
### `objective_state`

`objective_state(id: string, mission?: int) -> string?` · safe for belief · reactive

Where an objective of the game stands (13 §5.1): `hidden`, `active`, `done` or `failed`; null if the game has none of that id.

- `id` (string): The objective's id.
- `mission` (int, optional): The number of the mission it is part of; left out, one of the scenario's own.

Its result changes on `objective_changed`, `mission_started`.

<a id="party"></a>
### `party`

`party() -> list<entity>` · safe for belief · reactive

The characters the player plays in the game, in the order they were taken up: the last is the one played now (13 §9.3). Empty with no game.

Its result changes on `control_changed`.

<a id="played-for"></a>
### `played_for`

`played_for() -> real` · safe for belief

How long the game has run, in seconds of universal time since it began; 0 with no game.

<a id="scenario-id"></a>
### `scenario_id`

`scenario_id() -> string?` · safe for belief · reactive

The qualified id of the scenario being played (13 §3); null if none is.

Its result changes on `scenario_started`.

## Social

<a id="intervenes"></a>
### `intervenes`

`intervenes(a: entity, b: entity) -> bool?` · not in a mind context

Whether `a` holds toward `b`, as the persona it takes `b` for, a relation of a kind flagged `intervenes` above its default (15 §9.1): whether `a` is a candidate for windows opened against `b` (03 §7.1). Null if either is not an entity. Reads what `a` holds: for window kinds and world rules, not safe for belief.

- `a` (entity): Who would step in.
- `b` (entity): For whom.

## Space

<a id="believed-dir"></a>
### `believed_dir`

`believed_dir(viewer: any, from: any, to: any) -> list<int>?` · not in a mind context · reactive

`dir` as a character believes it, as `believed_dist` is `dist`: what `dir(from, to)` is compiled as in that character's mind context. Where that is held to truth, as an action's `requires` is when it starts, it is `dir(from, to)`.

- `viewer` (any): The character whose belief is read.
- `from` (any): Where the step starts.
- `to` (any): What it is toward.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="believed-dist"></a>
### `believed_dist`

`believed_dist(viewer: any, a: any, b: any) -> real?` · not in a mind context · reactive

`dist` as a character believes it: what `dist(a, b)` is compiled as in that character's mind context (05 §7.3). The character itself, and whatever it holds or is inside, is where it is; anyone else is where it believes them to be (`believed_loc`), null if it has no idea; cells, elements, areas and sites are where they are. Reads that character's beliefs, so it is not safe for belief itself. Where an expression compiled in a mind context is held to truth, as an action's `requires` is when it starts (03 §6.6), it is `dist(a, b)`.

- `viewer` (any): The character whose belief is read.
- `a` (any): One end.
- `b` (any): The other end.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="dir"></a>
### `dir`

`dir(from: any, to: any) -> list<int>?` · safe for belief · reactive

The step from one thing toward another: the signs of the shortest offset east, south and up, each -1, 0 or 1. Null where `dist` is null. In a mind context it is `believed_dir` with the character first.

- `from` (any): Where the step starts.
- `to` (any): What it is toward.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="dist"></a>
### `dist`

`dist(a: any, b: any) -> real?` · safe for belief · reactive

The distance between two things in metres, a storey counting three, the shorter way round on wrapped axes (02 §3.3). Each is a cell, an element, or something that is somewhere: an entity, an area (its middle), a site (its anchor). Null if either is nowhere or they are in different grids. In a mind context it is `believed_dist` with the character first: an entity is where the character believes it is.

- `a` (any): One end.
- `b` (any): The other end.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="light"></a>
### `light`

`light(at: any) -> real?` · not in a mind context

How bright a cell is now (15 §3.3). The same as its `light` property.

- `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.

<a id="los"></a>
### `los`

`los(a: any, b: any) -> bool?` · not in a mind context · reactive

Whether terrain leaves a clear line between two things, each as for `dist`, an entity seen from and at the height it stands at (02 §22). Null if either is nowhere, or the line comes to space that is not loaded before anything blocks it.

- `a` (any): One end.
- `b` (any): The other end.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`, `element_changed`.

<a id="offset"></a>
### `offset`

`offset(at: loc, dx: int, dy: int, dz?: int) -> loc?` · safe for belief

The cell so many cells east, south and up of a cell, wrapped on wrapped axes. Null beyond an edge of the realm.

- `at` (loc): The cell to start from.
- `dx` (int): Cells east.
- `dy` (int): Cells south.
- `dz` (int, optional): Storeys up. Zero if left out.

<a id="places"></a>
### `places`

`places(at: any, radius: real, interaction: string, except?: list<any>) -> list<element>` · safe for belief

The elements, blocks and fixtures, within `radius` metres of a cell (as `dist` measures, a storey counting three; at most 16) whose definition lists an interaction, nearest the cell first and then by cell (storey, row, column), leaving out those whose cell is in `except`: where a searcher goes to look (09 §4.1). Which elements stand where and what their definitions offer is static geometry (09 §3.4), known to every mind, so it is safe for belief; an element tagged `hidden` is not listed, nor is a cell that is not loaded. Not what state anything is in or what it holds. Empty for an interaction that is not loaded.

- `at` (any): The cell to look about, or an element (its cell). Null gives an empty list.
- `radius` (real): How far from it, in metres.
- `interaction` (string): The qualified id of the interaction (`core:search`).
- `except` (list<any>, optional): Cells, or elements by their cell, to leave out: those already searched.

## Windows

<a id="away-from"></a>
### `away_from`

`away_from(who: any, from: any) -> string?` · safe for belief

The step that leads straight away from `from` for `who`: `north`, `north_east`, `east`, `south_east`, `south`, `south_west`, `west` or `north_west`, by the signs of the shortest offset on the level. Null for two in one column, or either nowhere. What a reaction that leaves steps by (07 §5.2). Safe for belief, as `dir` is.

- `who` (any): Who steps: an entity or a cell.
- `from` (any): What it steps away from: an entity or a cell.

<a id="window-kind-of"></a>
### `window_kind_of`

`window_kind_of(window: window?) -> id<window_kind>?` · safe for belief

The kind of a window that is still open.

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-open"></a>
### `window_open`

`window_open(window: window?) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a window is still open (03 §7.1).

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-source"></a>
### `window_source`

`window_source(window: window?) -> entity?` · safe for belief

Whose action or rule opened a window that is still open; null for one that is closed or has no source. Safe for belief: a window is offered only to those who perceive its source (03 §7.2).

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-time-left"></a>
### `window_time_left`

`window_time_left(window: window?, who: entity) -> real?` · not in a mind context

Seconds of `who`'s own time before a window is expected to close: when the phase that opened it ends, where that phase leads straight to the one that closes it, or when its length is over. Null for a window that is closed or whose deadline is not known.

- `window` (window?): The window.
- `who` (entity): Whose own time it is counted in.
